source.version_note: Final published Public Administration Review 83(2):263–278, DOI 10.1111/puar.13602, 2023. Publisher first-online date 4 January 2023; copyright-line correction 6 February 2023. Includes Appendices A–E, including an image-only map page and experimental flow diagram.
source.verification_method: All 16 pages read, including references, all Appendices A–E, four main figures, every table, the two image-only appendix maps and the flow diagram. Visual inspection preserves minus signs lost in text extraction and distinguishes clustered GEE from independent-row robustness results. Publisher and Crossref checks verify identity and selected bibliography roles/volume. Raw data/code and OSF registration contents were not independently read or reproduced.

citation.title: ‘Just like I thought’: Street-level bureaucrats trust AI recommendations if they confirm their professional judgment

reading.source_scope_note: A Dutch police-officer vignette experiment compares congruent/incongruent mock recommendations and short local explanations. Reported 124 officers contribute 294 repeated vignette observations, not 294 independent people. Professional congruence is designed from qualitative input, not each officer’s independently elicited initial choice. Administrative discretion is a secondary governance definition. All supplied appendices were read; linked raw materials and original cited books were not.
access_limits: No raw dataset, analysis code, complete original survey, OSF record chronology or cited original book/study was independently read. Appendix D’s disclosed deviations are available in the supplied file and were read.

All image-only maps were visually inspected; the stabbing map labels both alternatives congruent, so intended labels must be reconciled with Table B1 and original survey rather than inferred as a raw coding error.
Reading a mock-system study does not establish real AI reliability, live deployment outcomes, model fairness or algorithmic explanation fidelity.

study.sampling: Four local department contacts distributed invitations to about 400 officers active or formerly active at street level. Data collected May to 3 June 2021: 152 respondents, 28 excluded for not completing at least one full scenario, reported final 124. Incomplete vignette completion plus an excluded fifth no-advice condition require trial-level flow to reconcile retained observations. Do not infer 98 respondents from 294/3. Ten lay pilot participants are separate from the officer analysis.
study.representation: Average reported age 47.9 and female share 25%, compared with workforce 45.2/34.7%. Ninety-three percent have executive status; remaining officers’ frontline experience is assumed from invitation criteria. This is a purposively accessed occupational sample, not independently verified random population representativeness or guaranteed applicability to all public officials.
study.design: Three randomly ordered crime scenarios: burglary toward a German border; ATM robbery in a fast car toward a highway; stabbing with a red car heading east. Per scenario, assignment to congruent/incongruent recommended location crossed with explained/unexplained. Local explanations supply plausible route rationales, not causal traces from an actual fitted model. Location, route plausibility and alignment change together; no objective offender route is observed.
study.congruence: Locations intended to align with professional knowledge were selected through qualitative police input. Manipulation asks alignment after the recommendation. No independently recorded individual pre-advice belief, calibrated uncertainty or correctness/fairness baseline exists. Rational use of geographical information and experience can therefore explain a congruence preference; the preference alone does not uniquely demonstrate motivated confirmation bias.
study.measures: Perceived trustworthiness combines correct information, correct recommendation, honest assessment, all relevant information and a direct trust item on 1–7 scales; alpha>.92 and one-component loadings>.74. This is a composite appraisal, not separately validated capability/integrity factors or measured actual accuracy. Binary adherence is selecting the recommended one of two locations in the survey, not live police conduct.
study.manipulations: Congruence check t=5.65, df=288.97, d=.64, p<.001; detail check t=3.34, df=262.47, d=.40, p<.001, each 294 rows. These checks describe perceived alignment/detail, not explanation fidelity or exact comprehension. Their independence treatment should be assessed against the repeated-person design. Realism mean 5.24/7 (SD1.25) supports perceived familiarity rather than establishing complete ecological validity.
study.counts_means: Table 3 incongruent unexplained N72, mean4.73, SD1.26; incongruent explained N90, mean4.98, SD1.17; congruent unexplained N56, mean5.26, SD1.10; congruent explained N76, mean5.25, SD1.18. These N sum to 294 vignette rows, not four groups of unique officers. Even incongruent means exceed the scale midpoint; the abstract’s only-trust wording is stronger than these descriptive results.
study.main_results: GEE congruence coding gives β=−.377, 95%[−.622,−.132], p=.003, consistent with lower trust for incongruent relative to congruent. Explanation coding β=−.133 [−.400,.134], p=.328; exploratory reported interaction β=−.259 [−.888,.371], p=.42. Minus signs are visible in the source but missing from extracted text. No significance is not equivalence, nor does comparing one significant effect with another nonsignificant effect prove their magnitudes differ.
study.trust_adherence: Logit GEE trustworthiness coefficient .243 [.006,.480], p=.045 (OR≈1.275 per scale unit), an association rather than a randomized trust effect. Appendix E independent-row logistic coefficient is also .243, SE .100, z2.420, p=.016, with intercept −.905, SE .518, z−1.748, p=.080; χ²6.001, p=.014. The different p values are compatible with different dependence assumptions, not a reporting contradiction or independent replication.
study.robustness: Appendix E1 independent-row ANOVA: explanation F1,290=1.03,p=.311; congruence7.39,p=.007; interaction.85,p=.357. Same qualitative decisions do not establish identical inference or replace the repeated-person GEE. GEE working correlation, missingness and scenario/carryover sensitivity require raw materials.
study.preregistration: Appendix D openly discloses rephrasing/restructuring hypotheses, dropping a fifth no-AI group and changing ordinary regressions to GEE to address within-person dependence. Original interactions were not maintained as hypotheses but are reported as nonsignificant. Trust→adherence H3 was added after unclear original specification. These are disclosed deviations, not hidden preregistered confirmations; no-AI removal particularly limits inference about automation effects versus unaided choices.
study.balance: General technology trust measured after experimental exposure differs across conditions (ANOVA p=.04), so it is not an unambiguous pre-treatment covariate imbalance. Table A1 uses repeated-row balance tests. Printed age F(3,280)=.182,p=.14 does not reconcile: conditional on that F/df, scipy’s reference tail is about .909. Preserve the discrepancy without guessing which original quantity is wrong.
study.visual_locators: Table 1 numbers incongruent unexplained as Group1, congruent unexplained Group2, incongruent explained Group3, congruent explained Group4; Appendix C numbers congruent versions Group1/3 instead. Condition labels and summed flow counts still reconcile (56/72/76/90), so this is a numbering conflict, not proof of different data. Appendix B stabbing map labels both A/B Congruent location, unlike the intended contrast. Appendix D calls the rephrased congruence hypothesis H2 though the main text/Figure1 make it H1.
study.scope: Results concern immediate mock-route choices and reported appraisals. No independently established police prejudice, algorithmic unfairness, real suspect route, caught offender, live harm reduction, long-term use or organizational safeguard is tested. Human oversight may help or hinder in theory, but both effects require their own outcome evidence.

summary: Add administrative discretion as a neutral institutional latitude, explicitly from a read secondary definition. Enrich confirmation bias, trust, contrastive-explanation and automation/selected-adherence boundaries without treating expertise-congruent choice as automatically irrational. Preserve the observed congruence effect, null explanation contrast and associative trust–adherence relationship; record disclosed deviations, actual sample structure, map/numbering conflicts, metadata corrections and the unresolved age statistic.

findings.definition: The latitude frontline public officials have to apply general policies to specific cases when choosing actions, sanctions or benefits.
findings.novelty_rationale: This is role-based latitude in policy implementation, distinct from subjective perceived autonomy, generic system control or moral independence from pressure. The current ontology has no named discretion construct.
findings.ai_evidence_status: A secondary institutional definition is explicitly discussed in the read article. The mock experiment does not measure lawful discretion or establish that an AI system legitimately holds public authority.
findings.ai_proposal: Specify policy rules, delegated authority and permitted case-level judgment, then test whether an AI-supported official or agent can adapt decisions to relevant local facts while staying within that authority and preserving reasons and review. Evaluate rights and actual decision quality separately from mere advice adherence.

evidence.quote: quantity, and quality of sanctions and rewards

findings.evidence_scope: The theory describes freedom to translate general rules and competing values into case-level choices, drawing on Lipsky and Tummers/Bekkers. This is institutional context, not a demonstrated cognitive bias or tested grant of AI authority. The original books/articles were not fully read or counted as independent evidence.
findings.boundary: Discretion can enable relevant contextual judgment or arbitrary/unfair action. Its presence is not inherently harmful or a license to disregard law, policy or scope. Perceived latitude, actual authorization, independent judgment and justified outcomes require separate evaluation.

findings.evidence_scope: Designed congruence with professional expectations increases trust ratings in 124 officers across 294 vignette rows. This is compatible with confirmation-based weighting, but location plausibility changes with congruence and individual prior beliefs/correct decisions are not independently measured.
findings.boundary: Evidence-congruent judgment can be rational. The source does not show police stereotypes, objectively worse route choices or a unique motivated mechanism; no-AI trials were excluded. A lower response to implausible advice does not establish that automation bias is absent.

findings.definition: Expecting an agent or system to perform competently and reliably in a relevant task.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named concept is already represented; add the read police-officer evidence and its limits without a duplicate synonym row.

findings.evidence_scope: A five-item composite covering information relevance, correctness, honesty and direct trust is higher for congruent recommendations. GEE trust–adherence coefficient .243 [.006,.480], p=.045 relates appraisals to binary mock-route choices. Even incongruent means remain above the 1–7 scale midpoint.
findings.boundary: Perceived capability is mixed with integrity/correctness endorsement and is not independently validated system reliability. Trust is not randomized and its association with choice does not establish causal mediation, calibrated reliance or live deployment behavior.

findings.novelty_rationale: The named concept is already represented; add the read police-officer evidence and its limits without a duplicate synonym row.

findings.evidence_scope: The article explicitly defines contrastive explanations as comparing the selected recommendation with an alternative, then supplies short local route rationales. Explained advice is judged more detailed; the trust contrast and explanation×congruence interaction are not significant.
findings.boundary: A route rationale is not proof of a faithful underlying model or objectively correct recommendation. Detail, comprehension, trust and warranted acceptance differ. A null result in this small mock study does not prove explanation ineffectiveness or equivalence.

findings.definition: A person’s judgment that a system’s operation or recommendations are understandable and can be explained.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named concept is already represented; add the read police-officer evidence and its limits without a duplicate synonym row.
findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: the explanation manipulation is checked using perceived detail, not the full perceived-explainability construct or independently measured comprehension. The trust outcome is a separate composite.
findings.boundary: More detailed text need not be understandable or faithful. The paper’s null explanation→trust contrast does not imply no change in understandability or zero effect of every XAI method.

findings.definition: Trusting a tool result or a prior step because a machine produced it, without verifying the load-bearing part.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named concept is already represented; add the read police-officer evidence and its limits without a duplicate synonym row.

findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: incongruent advice receives less trust and some officers reject it. The removed no-advice condition, lack of correctness ground truth and professional-plausibility manipulation do not establish an absence of excessive machine reliance.
findings.boundary: Unconditional following and harmful overreliance are distinct; selective acceptance may coexist with automation bias. The paper tests immediate mock recommendations, not long-term highly reliable automation or compared non-police domains.

findings.definition: Preferentially following advice when it matches prior stereotypes or beliefs about the person or group affected by a decision.
findings.novelty_rationale: The named concept is already represented; add the read police-officer evidence and its limits without a duplicate synonym row.
findings.evidence_scope: Boundary only: designed professional congruence influences trust. The study does not manipulate demographic stereotypes about an affected person or directly measure respondents’ prejudices, which the narrower selective-adherence definition requires.
findings.boundary: Do not turn expertise-based geographical judgments into evidence of discrimination without independently establishing a stereotype or unjustified selective treatment. General confirmation-compatible preference and stereotype-conditioned adherence are related but not identical.

methodological_limits: Congruent versus incongruent advice also changes task-relevant geographic plausibility. With no elicited pre-advice individual judgment or correct outcome, the experiment does not isolate unjustified confirmation, harmful rejection or fairer AI advice.

Dropped no-AI group and absent human-source comparison limit tests of automation-specific overreliance, algorithm preference and baseline belief change. Confirmation and automation bias need not be mutually exclusive.

Participants are real officers but choices are in a mock survey. Repeated rows, partial completions, selection through four contacts and assumed experience require caution about representative sampling and generalization.

The explanation manipulation increases perceived detail; it does not independently show comprehension, model fidelity, calibrated trust or actual fairness. A null contrast cannot establish no XAI effect under other designs or equivalence.

Trust is not independently randomized, and asking that the recommendation is correct overlaps with endorsing it. The trust–choice coefficient does not demonstrate a causal mediator or the psychological cause of adherence.

Main GEE accounts for person-level dependence; independent-row Appendix E and manipulation/balance tests need separate uncertainty treatment. Their different p values need not be errors. No missing-data/carryover/cluster sensitivity was independently reproduced.

Appendix D deviations are disclosed. Excluding inattentive checks alone does not define a complete intention-to-treat analysis, especially with incomplete outcomes and excluded no-advice trials. Do not equate lack of attention exclusions with automatically unbiased field effects.

Only contradictory labels/metadata are directly corrected. Reconcile raw age test, group numbering, original map stimuli and causal/model assumptions before replacing numerical results or claiming proven policy efficacy.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The large public aircraft task and this occupational route-choice task operationalize expertise differently. Neither a background-index curve nor a designed congruence contrast is a direct confidence-calibration measure; actual performance, justified evidence use and harmful reliance remain distinct.

Public observer blame of judges does not directly measure official advice use; this study observes mock choices by actual officers. These complementary designs cannot be merged into a single inference about real accountability or public-sector bias.

The error-repair study bundles explanation with history/context, while this study uses short route rationales. Neither supports a universal XAI benefit or absence; compare the exact information, task, outcomes and uncertainty.

deferred.reason: A domain-experience background is used to design plausible locations, but the paper does not independently define/test a separate new general mechanism beyond existing knowledge-guided advice weighting. Do not add a synonym for every domain variant.

These are cited governance-framework labels; the source gives a usable definition for administrative discretion, but the original cited frameworks were not fully read. Do not create additional unreviewed subtypes.
Technical explanation scope labels are not new psychological behaviors. The explicitly defined contrastive approach enriches the existing contrastive-explanation entry.

deferred.term: Human oversight necessarily corrects AI bias
deferred.reason: No real AI error/fairness outcome is tested. Keep the mechanism and institutional safeguards as proposed, context-dependent follow-ups.

limitations: The linked OSF data/materials and registration were not independently read; supplied Appendices A–E were fully read.
Bibliographic corrections do not imply full reading of O’Neil, Lipsky, Tummers/Bekkers or other original cited books/studies.

interpretation_qualifications.qualification: Minus signs lost by extraction are restored from the visual source: negative GEE contrasts and negative logistic intercept are not contradictory positive effects. GEE p=.045 versus independent-row logistic p=.016 reflects different uncertainty assumptions, not necessarily a typo.

Only trust / do not overturn / fair-AI-cannot-correct language is stronger than a congruence contrast with positive trust means and an uncertain explanation effect. Real correctness, fairness and individual pre-advice beliefs were not directly established.

Including respondents without attention exclusions does not by itself prove full ITT, representative sampling or unbiased real-world effects. Partial outcomes, the removed no-advice group and four-department access require explicit qualification.
